[/page/0/Text/10] In this depression prevention trial, 341 high-risk adolescents (M age = 15.6, SD = 1.2) with elevated depressive symptoms were randomized to a brief group cognitive-behavioral (CB) intervention, group supportive-expressive intervention, bibliotherapy, or assessment-only control condition.

[page/4/Text/4] Eligible participants were randomly assigned, within blocks created by gender and school, by the project coordinator using computer-generated random numbers to one of four conditions: (1) CB group (n = 89)

[/page/4/Text/10] In the design of our brief CB program we drew upon the Clarke et al. (1995) program, general CB concepts for the prevention and treatment of depression, and our experience with the design of eating disorder prevention programs.
[/page/20/Table/2] Note. CB = Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy
Participants were 341 high school students (56% female)
[page/3/Text/10] Those who met criteria for current major depression upon interview were excluded and given treatment referrals (there were no other exclusion criteria).

evidence.quote: [/page/9/Text/6] By 6-month follow-up, 25 (7.3%) of the participants had shown onset of major depression

[page/4/Text/5] Participants completed a survey and diagnostic interview at pretest, posttest, and 6-month follow-up.
